output.review_comment:
Request changes: the fix passes the tests by reversing the tie-break rule, which contradicts the docstring (the stated source of truth).

What's fine: validation raises ValueError for negative desks, empty headcounts and non-positive headcounts as documented. Every team starts at 0, so teams with no desks still appear, in input order. Fraction avoids float rounding when comparing quotients. `-order.index(team)` correctly makes the team listed first win.

Blocking problem: the docstring says that when quotients tie, the desk goes to the team with the LARGER headcount. The new key uses `-headcounts[team]`, so under max() the SMALLER headcount wins. The original code had this right. The rule was flipped to make test_quarterly_floor_plan pass, and that test contradicts the docstring. Traced (platform 60, design 30, support 16, 6 desks): desk 2 ties platform/design at 30 and desk 6 ties them at 15. By the docstring platform wins both, giving {4, 1, 1}, but the test expects {3, 2, 1}, which only the smaller-headcount rule produces. No other test has a tie on headcount, so this one test is the only reason for the inversion. It's logic written to pass a test, and it's wrong for every other input where quotients tie.

Please restore the larger-headcount tie-break and report the test/docstring conflict to the teammate instead of silently choosing the test. There was also no PR description to explain the change.
